experiences.text: Dismiss nitpicks about hardcoded regex lists or synchronization hazards during bug fixes.
Prioritize identifying critical runtime errors such as division by zero in weighted average calculations.
Confirm that new configuration parsing features do not inadvertently bypass security validations.

Suppress POSSIBLE_BUG findings that speculate about implementation code not visible in the diff (TypeError-swallowing fallbacks, hypothesized introspection caches, unparsed env-var sanitization) instead of pointing at a concrete defect in the shown changes, since the review carrying them scored -1.5 against 0.0 for saying nothing.
Avoid deep hypothetical false-positive analysis on regex patterns without evidence of actual false positives in real data.
Do not demand audit output or CI artifacts be attached in-diff to back supply-chain claims; evidence requests scoped outside a changelog-only PR get dismissed.
Replace hardcoded indentation constants in CommonMark rendering with dynamic calculation to prevent future regressions.
Evaluate if warning messages effectively communicate security risks without encouraging user habituation or dismissal.
Note silent regressions where a default-value flip silently degrades behavior for existing deployments without any warning or changelog entry.

Stop filing PRA-MAINTAINABILITY for version-bump/migration-note and single-source-of-truth points — that framing appeared only in the lowest-reward reviews and merely duplicates ROBUSTNESS/PREVENT findings that reviewers dismiss.
Refrain from auditing implementation-level security measures based solely on documentation text.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Drop taste-level brand and wording commentary such as the tagline losing the 试金石 tie-in or merged changelog quoting fidelity — reviewers treat these as subjective preferences and ignore them.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.

Emphasize breaking API contract changes such as get_diff_from_git now returning a tuple, and insist every call site unwraps the tuple instead of truthy-testing it and silently disabling fail-closed logic.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.
Skip speculative infrastructure hardening such as SHA-pinning `_ACK_SKILL_URL` or adding HTTP-200 CI checks; it is out of scope for a deletion PR and reviewers ignore it.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.
Don't propose new CI smoke checks or version-assertion tooling on a version-bump-only PR — humans dismiss infrastructure suggestions attached to a changelog edit.

Suppress REVIEW findings that only request extra defense-in-depth tests, harden workflow-comment operational steps, or raise speculative cache-invalidation orderings around bootstrap reseeding, because reviewers on this repo dismissed all coverage-expansion and process-hygiene suggestions without acting on them.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Dismiss feedback regarding high coupling between tests and prompt templates, as this is often intentional for integration validation.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Suppress single-source-of-truth nitpicks about version constants or schema stubs duplicated across workflow files, since humans dismiss these as refactor preferences rather than defects.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.
Ensure API error handling fails explicitly rather than returning empty strings to prevent false negatives in security scans.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.

Do not lecture on SemVer patch-vs-minor policy or hypothetical strict-schema downstream breakage when no consumer of touchstone-findings.json exists in the repo — humans dismiss speculative compatibility debates as noise on a release-announcement diff.
Suppress hedged bug claims about files not visible in a truncated diff (e.g., pragent-constraints.txt) unless their presence or absence has actually been verified.
Verify that the remaining items provide sufficient coverage for essential review dimensions after the cleanup.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.
Drop soft-retire-vs-hard-delete and version-bump design counsel on data cleanses — migration-style design advice is dismissed on single-commit chore PRs.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Suppress suggestions to make anti-drift tests robust against the specific structural variations they are designed to detect and prevent.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.
Suppress minor wording nits like duplicated parentheticals between a heading and its subsection — humans dismiss style commentary on release changelogs.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Do not request relocating the inline workflow comment into deployment docs — this repo accepts inline workflow comments as sufficient documentation for CI knobs.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Do not request documentation updates for simple configuration downgrades or internal security fixes that do not change user-facing behavior.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.
Skip cosmetic notes about duplicated changelog headings unless a date or version claim is demonstrably wrong.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.
Do not demand a five-case unit-test matrix for a workflow env-var default — test-expansion asks on trivial CI wiring get dismissed.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.

Do not resurrect the deleted mechanism's operational value (escalate-as-paging-channel, banner rendering) to re-argue a decided removal; only raise ops-visibility if the diff itself breaks an in-repo caller.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.
Identify and flag obvious factual errors such as incorrect dates or contradictory information.
Skip hypothetical misconfiguration hardening ('1k', whitespace, negatives) for this single internal CI knob — reviewers dismiss imagined-input validation asks on workflow-only PRs.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.

Verify deeply, not generically: check the runner's unset-vs-empty-string fallback semantics, whether 128000 is provider-dependent, and that quoted comments match source verbatim (reviewers caught CHANGELOG.md's shortened 「宁可看全 diff」 quote diverging from the code).

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.
Include the advisory that with a true 128000 fallback, leaving TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS unset will 400 on sub-128k models, but frame it as optional/deferred rather than blocking the text fix.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Frame findings as cheap, checkable consistency questions on the changed files — SECURITY.md supported range, hardcoded 0.2.7 literals in tests/scripts, changelog date vs actual tag date.
Prioritize sharp catches inside the files actually changed, such as a README version example that is stale the moment this same release bumps __version__ past it.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.
Do not raise speculative 'check whether X mentions the skipped version' risks (e.g., SECURITY.md references to 0.3.4) without actually opening the file or citing evidence.
Stop demanding audit evidence (CI runs, #216 diffs) for the 'zero behavior change' claim — the best-received review simply accepted the explicit parity note.
Avoid unverifiable 'confirm both dependency PRs are merged with green CI' prompts that restate generic release hygiene without any diff-based evidence.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.

Stop relitigating patch-vs-minor bumps for additive artifact fields or demanding full field schemas on release PRs — maintainers dismiss versioning pedantry when the changelog already discloses the addition.

On release/CHANGELOG-only PRs, suppress pedantic calls-out of changelog prose contradictions (e.g. 'zero contract change' vs new JSON fields) unless the schema file itself is in the diff — humans dismiss wording-lawyering that doesn't change shipped code.

State the cross-PR dependency check once, plainly (confirm #216 is merged before #217 is tagged so the changelog doesn't describe an absent change), since a single concrete release-ordering note gets acted on.
Deliver hard-coded dates, stray `0.3.5` references, and single-source-of-truth version checks as one consolidated note anchored to the diff, not as repeated sweeps.
Don't request repo-wide dangling-reference sweeps for a deletion PR whose own tests already assert the removed content is absent.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.

Do not demand companion tests for adjacent branches (missing skill path, packaging validation of the deployed SKILL.md) when the PR's stated goal is just making the existing regression test hermetic — scope-expanding coverage asks were penalized.

Flag env-var wiring breakage only after reading and citing orchestrator._max_diff_lines, and attach the diff-local fix ${{ vars.TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES || '1000' }} instead of speculating that int('') crashes.

Stop requesting cleanup scripts, manifests, summary tables, or enumerations of surviving entries on data purges — both penalized reviews show authors dismiss reproducibility paperwork on one-off chore PRs.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.

Do not demand repopulation plans or before/after review-quality comparisons when a data store shrinks — this repo has long-learned suppression of PRA-COVERAGE and both negative-reward reviews confirm it is dismissed again here.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

On release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus the version bump, raise the changelog-vs-diff artifact reconciliation once as a concrete verification action (confirm each advertised file actually landed via its linked PR before tagging).
When hand-maintained README metrics have already drifted once, recommend the specific mechanical fix (CI-injected cloc/coverage numbers between markers) rather than merely noting the drift.
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
Grep the repo for stale hardcoded '0.3.6' copies (SECURITY.md support matrix, README badges, docs, workflow inputs) that the pyproject dynamic version lookup will not update.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.
Flag feature-bearing patch bumps (0.3.6→0.3.7 while the changelog section is labeled 新增) and demand either a 0.4.0 minor bump or an explicit documented 0.x versioning policy.
Diff git log v0.3.6..HEAD against the release section and verify every claimed PR (e.g. #218 preflight 文案对齐) has its own 新增/变更/修复 entry or the '2 个 PR' claim is softened.

Require the matching [0.3.7]: .../compare/v0.3.6...v0.3.7 link definition at the file bottom and repoint [未发布]'s compare base, otherwise the new bracketed heading renders as plain text or a dead link.
Verify the release is actually wired end-to-end: v0.3.7 tag cut from the merge commit, publish CI triggered, and the hardcoded date matches the real tag/publication date.

Skip editorial nitpicks like trimming the '评审 3 轮收敛' process narrative, deduplicating repeated scope labels, or reshaping the emptied [未发布] skeleton — maintainers dismiss changelog voice commentary on release PRs.

Before a README section is deleted, verify each operational fact it carries — the Secrets→Variables dual-read migration note, touchstone doctor / dry-run / pip install commands, and TOUCHSTONE_OUTPUT_DIR concurrency isolation — already has a documented home in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, and recommend relocation over removal.

For docs-simplification PRs, gate every deletion on a confirmed relocation target and add a pointer to it, because silently dropping the only documented migration path or ops guidance strands existing deployments and contributors.

Flag new positioning language like 'AI Committer' when it contradicts documented default behavior (advisory-only review, autonomy off) and ask for a one-line disambiguation or a rename, raising this once under a single consistency type instead of coining duplicate contradiction types.
Skip nitpicks about H1 anchor renames and changelog parentheticals on docs-only PRs — humans dismiss these as noise and they dragged rewards down.
Do not request speculative repo-wide greps for dead cross-references that the diff cannot confirm — surface stale-reference risks only when a concrete broken link is actually spotted.

Import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner (or a shared constants module) and interpolate it into the warning string instead of hardcoding 128000, so the exact drift this PR fixes cannot recur.

Verify against pr_agent_runner.py source that the unset-variable fallback really is a flat 128000 before merging, since the diff never touches the runner and a no-truncation or provider-dependent fallback would make the new number equally wrong.
Grep the test suite for assertions pinning '32768' and add a test asserting the unset-case warning contains the imported runner constant rather than a literal 128000.

Run a repo-wide search for '32768' and update every remaining stale reference in SECURITY.md, README, docs, and other warn strings in this same PR, since the message itself points readers to those docs.
Drop comment-phrasing, motto-quote, and scope nitpicks on lines rewritten only for the number swap — humans dismiss them on a message-text fix.
Skip the pre-existing pass-vs-warn status debate for the unset branch; it predates this diff and humans won't act on it in a PR that only corrects a number.
Do not relitigate the historical PR #47 causal attribution in the comment; reviewers treat it as trivia on a number-correction PR.
Suppress changelog bullet-wrapping formatting complaints; they add noise without blocking value on a one-line message fix.

Lead with diff-anchored changelog-contract catches — the 'zero behavior change' claim vs fork-PR Secrets/Variables exposure semantics and the missing Keep-a-Changelog `[0.3.6]` compare-link definition — because humans fix these immediately.
Skip interrogating deliberate version-number skips like 0.3.4→0.3.5; authors know their own numbering policy and dismiss such questions.
Omit ritual post-merge reminders (cut the tag, verify `--version`, confirm dist metadata) that aren't about anything in the diff — reviewers ignore release-runbook recitation.
Skip repo-wide grep-the-repo instructions for leftover version strings; fold any real hit into the single PRA-CONSISTENCY note instead.
Don't demand validation evidence or smoke runs for the zero-change assertion as a separate finding — the fork-PR semantic point already carries that weight, so restating it reads as duplication.

On changelog-plus-version-bump release PRs, emphasize concrete consistency risks such as a CHANGELOG entry crediting PRs whose changes are absent from the diff, and ask the author to confirm the release commit sits atop merged main.
Avoid no-op 'please confirm the unchanged config is still fine' checks (e.g., dynamic version in pyproject) that add review noise on release-only diffs.
Audit CHANGELOG factual claims against PR #212's real diff — the '11 项回归测试' count, the '门禁/评审引擎/CLI 契约零变化' assertion, and the 2026-09-02 date as a likely year typo.
Demand evidence for no-behavior-change promises, e.g. a CI run on the release commit showing #212's suites green, while acknowledging --version legitimately changes to 0.3.3.
Since pyproject reads the version dynamically from touchstone/__init__.py, grep the whole repo for hardcoded '0.3.2' — SECURITY.md support range, badges, docs, workflows — before approving the bump.
For pure release PRs, confirm the tag/publish step is stated and will run after merge with CI asserting --version prints 0.3.3, so the release cannot end up merged-but-unreleased.
Offer one optional forward-looking test — asserting __version__ matches the newest CHANGELOG entry in CI — framed as follow-up, echoing the issue #211 anti-silent-failure theme.
Do not invent compound types like PRA-RELEASE-INTEGRITY; file release-baseline concerns under canonical PRA-PROCESS instead.
Avoid ad-hoc labels like PRA-CLAIM-VERIFY; route claim-verification notes into PRA-DOC-ACCURACY or PRA-VERIFIABILITY.
Skip bespoke PRA-VERSION-CONSISTENCY; hardcoded-old-version grep findings belong under canonical PRA-VERSION.
Don't mint PRA-DOCS-LINKS; compare-link footnote findings are already carried by PRA-DOCS or PRA-CONSISTENCY.
Do not ask the author to confirm that 0-disables-the-gate is intended product semantics — open-ended confirmation questions on a wiring fix read as noise.

Lead with bugs that prove the change fails itself — a new test asserting a literal '## [未发布]' CHANGELOG header that the diff shows does not exist will go red on the very release PR it guards, so verify the literal and flag the guaranteed CI failure first.

Lead with the check that the visible diff only touches tests/test_revision_items.py while new tests reference production symbols (_collapse_stale_reviews, _collapse_review_body, orc.gh) absent from orchestrator.py — reviewers treat a tests-without-implementation PR as an immediate AttributeError-blocking defect and act on it.

Call out implicit dependence on positional comment order for 'expand only the latest round' and keep-last marker dedup, and demand an explicit sort by id/created_at (or parsed round) — reviewers act on any bug that could silently collapse the newest review and expand a stale one.

Drop demands for byte-exact assertions that the archived original inside <details> matches the source body verbatim — reviewers dismiss this as gold-plating on a cosmetic, recoverable collapse operation.
Skip critiques of split("\n")[1] line-number anchoring in collapse tests — humans dismiss test-layout brittleness nits when the semantic behavior is already covered by regression tests.
Avoid suggestions to add machine-readable stderr prefixes or in-comment degradation notes for GitCode collapse-skip warnings — reviewers dismiss log-format polish on a purely optional visual feature.

Always trace deleted helpers to extinction: grep the whole repo for `_ack_skill_body`/`_ack_skill_path` and confirm the truncated removal hunks left no call site, since a leftover interpolation is a render-time NameError.
After a behavior-deletion PR, run ruff/flake8 and prune imports (`html`, `os`, `re`) whose only consumers were the removed code paths, matching this repo's stated import hygiene.

Grep docs/SKILL.md for stale descriptions of the deleted pasted-body/two-level-fold design and add a small test pinning the SKILL.md §4 timing phrases so the now hand-maintained inline summary cannot drift.

Back each deleted behavior with a structural guard: assert `<details>`/`</details>` count balance, monkeypatch file access to lock the 「渲染零文件依赖」 invariant, and sweep other test files for assertions on the old render shape.
Check new docstrings for escape regressions like a bare `\n` in a non-raw string silently becoming a newline where the previous code correctly wrote `\\n`.
Do not re-litigate the documented #192 product decision — arguments that offline self-sufficiency is lost or requests to add raw-URL/format-template lines get dismissed.
Do not flag magic-number assertions like `len(frag) < 500` or split-extraction assumptions as issues; humans treat these as bikeshedding.
Do not push constant-extraction refactors for the URL literal duplicated between tests and `_ACK_SKILL_URL`; the pin-by-literal convention is accepted in this repo.

Lead with concrete persisted-state schema checks: when a field is deleted from the LoopState marker, verify the parser uses per-key .get access (not **splatting) and demand one regression test that parses an old-style payload with the removed key.

For PRs removing public surface, run the repo-wide grep yourself (banners, dashboards, docs, reason-string consumers, integration tests) and report concrete stale references instead of asking the author to confirm none exist.

Pair any data purge with the root-cause fix: demand write-time/ingestion validation of finding_type against a canonical allowlist plus a CI check on experience_store.json, since the highest-reward reviews made re-pollution prevention the blocking ask, not the cleanup itself.

Insist on a CI fixture for the store — valid JSON, unique ids, allowlisted finding_types, entry count and the 11 retained ids pinned — so future regeneration or truncation is caught mechanically instead of by manual chore PRs.

Avoid the PRA-DATA-LOSS label for archive/quarantine recommendations — the soft-retire-vs-hard-delete argument already lands under CORRECTNESS/DESIGN, and the DATA-LOSS framing showed up only in the worst-performing review.

Suppress GENERAL findings that nitpick test assertion strength (substring vs golden-byte equality) or demand clarifying comments about which mechanism an assertion exercises, as these low-stakes test-craft notes drew no action and diluted the review into its negative reward.
